subject.title: fix(security): ignore string-literal contents in code-safety env/exfil rules (#82469)

question: Should `env-harvesting` and `potential-exfiltration` treat string-literal contents as non-code while relying on other scanner rules for string payloads and dynamic execution?
rationale: This is a focused bug fix, but it changes the detection boundary of a security-audit scanner, so automation should not decide that policy tradeoff alone.

options.title: Accept literal masking for env/exfil
options.body: Land the PR once exact-head checks finish, keeping file coverage intact and treating quoted text as data for these two code-construct rules.

options.title: Require another guard first
options.body: Ask for one more regression around dynamic-code or string payload coverage if maintainers want stronger proof before accepting the boundary.

options.title: Pause for scanner policy
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want env/exfil heuristics to continue inspecting string payloads despite the false positives.

recommendation.title: Accept literal masking for env/exfil
recommendation.body: Land the PR once exact-head checks finish, keeping file coverage intact and treating quoted text as data for these two code-construct rules.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and release-line history put this account closest to the current scanner implementation and security-audit path.
